findings.title: Handle a missing TopicUser row in unsubscribe
Provide unsubscribe_url to every email using unsubscribe_link, or make the topic sentence conditional
Stop changing notification state on a CSRF-able GET request
Client-side unsubscribe route shows message without performing the unsubscribe
Make unsubscribe wording match the level actually set
Use TopicUser.change instead of saving the record directly
Avoid rendering interpolated topic title as raw HTML

response: ## 1) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Consensus: 3/3 reviewers Title: Handle a missing TopicUser row in unsubscribe Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105-113 Explanation: `TopicUser.find_by(...)` returns `nil` when the logged-in user has no `topic_users` row for the topic. This happens in several realistic cases: - The user was notified through category watching, a group, or a mention without ever visiting the topic. - The email was forwarded to someone else. - A different account is logged in than the email's recipient. In each case `tu.notification_level` raises `NoMethodError`, and the unsubscribe link from the email returns a 500. Fix: treat a missing row (or nil level) as `regular`, and write the change through `TopicUser.change`, which upserts the row. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: @topic_view.topic.id) current = tu.try(:notification_level) || TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] new_level = current > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] ? TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular] : TopicUser.notification_levels[:muted] TopicUser.change(current_user.id, @topic_view.topic.id, notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 2) Severity: HIGH | Type: Bug Consensus: 3/3 reviewers Title: Provide unsubscribe_url to every email using unsubscribe_link, or make the topic sentence conditional Affected: - config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855 - lib/email/message_builder.rb:24-28 - lib/email/message_builder.rb:67 Explanation: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` renders this string for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, but only `UserNotifications#send_notification_email` passes `unsubscribe_url`. Other mailers, such as digests, are outside this diff and should be verified. For those other emails, `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` will either: - raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`, so the email fails to send, or - render a broken "click here" link. Even when it renders, the "this particular topic" sentence makes no sense in non-topic emails. The spec had to add `unsubscribe_url` to keep passing, which shows the new coupling. Fix: keep the original key unchanged, add a separate per-topic key, and append it only when `unsubscribe_url` is present. Proposed fix: ~~~yaml unsubscribe_link: "To unsubscribe from these emails, visit your [user preferences](%{user_preferences_url})." unsubscribe_link_topic: "To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url})." ~~~ ~~~ruby unsubscribe_text = I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) if template_args[:unsubscribe_url].present? unsubscribe_text << "\n\n" << I18n.t('unsubscribe_link_topic', template_args) end unsubscribe_link = PrettyText.cook(unsubscribe_text).html_safe ~~~ ## 3) Severity: HIGH | Type: Security Consensus: 3/3 reviewers Title: Stop changing notification state on a CSRF-able GET request Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98-116 - config/routes.rb:440-441 Explanation: `topics#unsubscribe` is routed as GET, with `check_xhr` skipped, yet it writes to the database. GET requests carry no CSRF token, so any third-party page or an `` embedded in a post can change a logged-in visitor's notification level on any topic they can see. Requests can also arrive without the user intending them: - email link scanners - browser prefetch - page reloads The action toggles rather than setting a fixed level (watching → regular, then regular → muted). Repeated hits therefore ratchet the user down to muted. The permanent 301 redirect onto this state-changing URL can be cached by browsers, which makes this worse. Fix: - Make GET render a confirmation page only. - Perform the change through a CSRF-protected POST/PUT, such as the existing notification-level endpoint used by `topic-notifications-button`. - Use a 302 instead of a 301 for the slug redirect. - If one-click unsubscribe from email is required, use a signed per-user token and an idempotent target level. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby # routes.rb get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe", constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/} # render only post "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#perform_unsubscribe", constraints: {topic_id: /\d+/} # controller def perform_unsubscribe topic_view = TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user) TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_view.topic.id, notification_level: TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]) # idempotent render json: success_json end ~~~ ## 4) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Consensus: 2/3 reviewers Title: Client-side unsubscribe route shows message without performing the unsubscribe Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:4-10 Explanation: The Ember route only calls `PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)`, which fetches the normal topic JSON and never hits the server `unsubscribe` action. The state change therefore happens only on a full-page HTML load from the email. When the route is reached through in-app navigation, the page says "You will stop receiving notifications…" but nothing changes. Fix: have the route call the CSRF-protected unsubscribe endpoint (see issue 3) before loading the topic. Proposed fix: ~~~js model(params) { const topic = this.store.createRecord("topic", { id: params.id }); return Discourse.ajax(`/t/${params.id}/unsubscribe`, { type: "POST" }) .then(() => PostStream.loadTopicView(params.id)) .then(json => { topic.updateFromJson(json); return topic; }); } ~~~ ## 5) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Doc Consensus: 2/3 reviewers Title: Make unsubscribe wording match the level actually set Affected: - config/locales/client.en.yml:985 - config/locales/server.en.yml:1855 - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-111 Explanation: Both the email and the page tell users they will stop receiving notifications for the topic. For watching or tracking users, however, the controller only lowers the level to `regular`, where replies and mentions still notify. The page never shows the resulting level, so users are misled about what happened. Fix: either always mute, or word the text around the resulting level. Proposed fix: ~~~yaml stop_notifications: "You will now receive fewer notifications for {{title}}." ~~~ ## 6) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Bug Consensus: 1/3 reviewers Title: Use TopicUser.change instead of saving the record directly Affected: - app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-113 Explanation: Saving `tu` directly with `tu.save!` bypasses the logic in `TopicUser.change`: - No `notification_level_change` MessageBus message is published, so open tabs keep showing the old level. - Notification-reason bookkeeping (`notifications_changed_at`, `notifications_reason_id`) is not updated, so the reason shown to the user becomes stale. Fix: route the change through `TopicUser.change`. Proposed fix: ~~~ruby TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id].to_i, notification_level: new_level) ~~~ ## 7) Severity: MEDIUM | Type: Security Consensus: 1/3 reviewers Title: Avoid rendering interpolated topic title as raw HTML Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7 Explanation: `model.fancyTitle` is interpolated into an I18n string, and the template renders the result unescaped with `{{{ }}}`. Client-side `I18n.t` does not escape interpolations. This is safe only if every code path that populates `fancyTitle` returns server-escaped HTML. Otherwise it becomes stored XSS on a page that users reach directly from email. Fix: escape the title before interpolating it. Proposed fix: ~~~js stopNotificiationsText: function() { return I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: Handlebars.Utils.escapeExpression(this.get("model.title")) }); }.property("model.title"), ~~~ ## 8) Severity: LOW | Type: Maintainability Consensus: 1/3 reviewers Title: Fix misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText Affected: - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/topic-unsubscribe.js.es6:5-7 - app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3 Explanation: "Notificiations" is misspelled. The controller and template currently agree with each other, but any future reference that uses the correct spelling will silently render nothing. Fix: rename the property in both places. Proposed fix: ~~~js stopNotificationsText: function() { ... }.property("model.fancyTitle") ~~~ ~~~hbs {{{stopNotificationsText}}} ~~~

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate: TopicUser.find_by returns nil when user has no topic_users row for the topic, causing NoMethodError on tu.notification_level and returning a 500 error on unsubscribe
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same issue: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when no record exists, and calling methods on the nil result (tu.notification_level) will cause an error. The golden comment describes it as a 'nil pointer exception' that will 'crash', while the candidate describes it as 'NoMethodError' causing a '500 error'. These are the same underlying bug - accessing methods on a potentially nil TopicUser object.

true_positives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')
true_positives.matched_candidate: Property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText), which will cause future references using correct spelling to silently render nothing
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies exactly the same typo as the golden comment - 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText'. Both point out the misspelling where 'Notifications' is incorrectly spelled as 'Notificiation' (missing 'n'). The candidate even provides additional context about the potential impact of this typo.
